name: How do commercial renovation costs change for older buildings in Pasadena?

mainEntity.name: How do commercial renovation costs change for older buildings in Pasadena or Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How do commercial renovation costs change for older buildings in Pasadena or Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older commercial buildings often cost more to renovate than newer construction because the existing conditions are less predictable. Once demolition starts, contractors may uncover outdated electrical systems, plumbing limitations, structural repairs, water damage, unlevel slabs, or finishes that no longer meet current standards. In some cases, the project may also require accessibility or fire/life safety upgrades that were not part of the original plan. This is especially relevant in older parts of Pasadena, Los Angeles, and nearby commercial corridors where buildings may have been renovated multiple times over the years. Owners should expect more contingency on historic or older structures and should avoid budgeting only from surface-level observations. A thorough preconstruction walk-through, existing-conditions review, and realistic allowance for hidden work can prevent project delays. The more complete the initial investigation, the fewer surprises appear after demolition. Older buildings are still good candidates for renovation, but they require tighter planning and more flexibility in both budget and schedule.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older commercial buildings usually cost more to renovate because hidden issues are more likely to appear during demolition. Common surprises include outdated wiring, undersized plumbing, damaged framing, asbestos-related concerns, uneven floors, and code upgrades. Budgeting extra contingency is often necessary in older properties.
